architecture: Server discovery and browser station validation now call the same parseMediaUrl helper from media-policy.ts. It inspects the original HTTPS authority before normalization, rejects colon-bearing authorities, then applies parsed URL credential, fragment, playlist and exact-origin checks. The shared nine-origin list, country-v9 resource, empty connectDomains and fixed-player CSP remain as previously reviewed.
complexity: A single shared parser removes duplicated validation and fixes the finding without broadening the change. The dated coverage document remains truthful about direct-byte observations and absent host playback evidence. No further code revision is requested by Review.
correctness: The raw-authority check rejects :443 before URL can erase it, as well as nondefault ports and malformed authority separators. Both callers use the shared result; browser validation also retains the source-origin equality requirement. Reviewed the candidate diff and baseline source-file list: no player, controller, coordinator, pagination generation/request guard, catalog append/reset, or override changes. The narrow validator consolidation is consistent with the approved rejection correction.
requirements: Reviewed exact candidate and attempt-2 packet; HEAD equals the full candidate SHA and PRODUCT/TECH hashes still match approved revisions. The previous explicit-default-port finding is resolved. Approval scope remains exactly two added media origins, no added UUID overrides, preserved DIAL-006 behavior, and separate Verify/owner host evidence gates. ACCEPT is code-review acceptance, not eight-country playback or hosting acceptance.
security: No wildcard origin, arbitrary URL input, proxy or added override appears. Existing signed provider UUID attribution remains unchanged. The earlier issue was a literal policy mismatch on an approved origin and is now corrected. Source validation does not establish runtime redirect destinations or host CSP/audibility; those remain explicit Verify obligations.
tests: Independently ran direct imports of the candidate TypeScript media-policy source with assertions for both new origins: ordinary URLs accepted and :443, :0443, :8443 and empty explicit port rejected. Independently ran node --test test/discovery.test.js test/station-list.test.js against existing build output; both test files passed. Inspected regression additions for both origins' :443 rejection in discovery and browser, retained :8443 checks, malformed-authority rejection and credential rejection. Full build/35-test suite pass is Implement evidence in the packet, not a fresh Review full-suite run; independent Verify still owns that gate.
